stories.headline: Nvidia's revenue doubles, but its shares stay far below their peak
stories.question: Nvidia doubled its revenue, so is the AI sell-off over or only paused?
stories.dek: Nvidia beat forecasts and raised its outlook, yet its shares barely moved. Strong results alone may not end the sell-off. Investors are also weighing a leadership crisis and opaque AI financing.

so_far.text: Nvidia's shares have a 52-week high of $243.37, but an AI sell-off has pulled them far below it. On 12 November chief executive Jensen Huang resigned. Colette Kress, the finance chief, became interim CEO, and a board investigation is ongoing. On 16 November two officials at the US Federal Reserve, the central bank, spoke about AI risks. On 17 November the S&P 500 fell 1.03% to about 7,341, extending the slide before Nvidia reported.

what_happened.text: On 17 November Nvidia reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $115.8bn. That is about double a year earlier and above the roughly $109bn analysts expected. Data-centre revenue hit a record $107.6bn. Nvidia forecast about $130bn for the next quarter, against analyst models of $124.9bn. It added $150bn to its buyback plan, money set aside to repurchase its own shares. Its chairman said the board does not intend to reinstate Huang. The shares had closed at $155.46, down 0.44%. After hours they rose by about 1.3% to 3%, depending on the report.

steps.text: A share price reflects expected future profits, so the roughly $109bn revenue forecast was already built into Nvidia's price.
Nvidia beat that estimate and guided about $130bn next quarter, which supports the case that AI demand is still growing.
But investors also weigh risk: a CEO who resigned, a board investigation, and gross margin guided down to 71–72%.
Fed Governor Michael Barr says opacity around more than $3tn of possible AI obligations can make sell-offs worse.
So strong results support the price, but whether the sell-off ends depends on whether those fears fade.

history.text:
Nvidia was founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem. In 1999 it listed its shares and launched the GeForce 256, marketed as the first GPU, or graphics processing unit: a chip that does many small calculations at once.

The real turning point came next. Nvidia spent over $1bn on CUDA, software launched in 2006 that let GPUs run general programs, not just graphics. That made its chips useful far beyond games. In 2012 an AI model called AlexNet was trained on Nvidia GPUs using CUDA, and CUDA became the base for AI training. In 2016 Nvidia gave OpenAI an early AI supercomputer, helping lay the groundwork for ChatGPT.

In October 2022 the US restricted exports of advanced AI chips to China, including Nvidia's data-centre chips. Then ChatGPT reached 100m monthly users in January 2023, the fastest consumer app growth on record. Demand for AI chips surged. In October 2025 Nvidia became the first company worth $5tn.

Borrowing grew with the boom. Debt tied to advanced computing passed $680bn by October 2026, about five times the $130bn issued in 2023. Then the sell-off came, and on 12 November 2026 Huang resigned.

lesson.concept: Why a share can fall while profits double
lesson.big_idea: A share price is profit per share times a multiple: how much investors will pay for each rupee of profit. Profits can double, but if fear shrinks the multiple, the price can still fall.

steps.title: A share is a slice
steps.text: Owning a share means owning a slice of a company's future profits. Investors pay now for profits they expect later, so the price is really a bet on the future.

steps.title: Meet the multiple
steps.text: The price-to-earnings multiple is the share price divided by one year's profit per share. A multiple of 50 means buyers pay ₹50 for each ₹1 of yearly profit.

steps.title: Expected news is already priced
steps.text: Analysts publish forecasts, and prices adjust to them in advance. Nvidia was expected to report about $109bn of revenue, so only the gap above that, to $115.8bn, was real news.

steps.title: Fear shrinks the multiple
steps.text: When investors worry about risk, they pay less for each rupee of profit. Nvidia's CEO resigned on 12 November, and a Fed governor warned opacity can worsen sell-offs.

steps.title: Price equals profit times multiple
steps.text: Put the pieces together: price = profit per share × multiple. If profit rises but the multiple falls faster, the price drops. Both pieces matter, not just the results.

example.setup: Say you own shares in a chip company that earns ₹10 profit per share each year. Investors are excited, so they pay 50 times that profit.

apply.text: Nvidia's revenue about doubled to $115.8bn, beating the $109bn estimate. Yet the shares closed on 17 November at $155.46, about 36% below their 52-week high of $243.37. Reports give no figure for Nvidia's multiple. But one likely explanation, in our formula, is that the multiple shrank as investors weighed Huang's resignation and Barr's warning on opaque AI financing.

practice.q: Same company: profit doubles to ₹20, but the multiple falls only to 30. What is the new price? At what multiple would you break even?
practice.answer: New price = ₹20 × 30 = ₹600. That is ₹100 more than ₹500, a 20% gain. To break even you need ₹500: ₹500 ÷ ₹20 = 25. Any multiple above 25 means you gain.

takeaways: A share price is profit times a multiple; fear can shrink the multiple faster than profit grows.
Nvidia's revenue doubled and beat forecasts, yet shares stay far below their peak while investors weigh leadership and financing risks.

stories.headline: US rule targets rented AI chips and resale routes to China
stories.question: How is Washington closing the back doors Chinese firms use to get American AI chips?
stories.dek: A US rule in force since 16 November makes overseas data centres identify Chinese users. It also adds licensing for five countries seen as risky resale routes.

so_far.text: Since August 2022 the US has required licences to sell advanced AI chips to China. By November 2026, attention had turned to how Chinese firms still get restricted chips. Reports focused on Megaspeed, a Singapore-based Nvidia buyer. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing. On 4 November three House committee chairs asked for a briefing from Nvidia's chief executive, Jensen Huang. Semafor reported separate Justice Department inquiries into Nvidia, Megaspeed and Supermicro. Neither the Justice Department nor Nvidia has confirmed them.

what_happened.text: On 16 November 2026 the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), the Commerce Department unit that runs export controls, issued rules limiting remote access to advanced US chips and servers. AP reported the rule took effect immediately. Overseas data centres serving companies in China, Russia, Iran and Cuba must now identify their end users. Chip sales to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil face added licensing. The rule treats those five as at higher-than-normal risk of diversion. Separately, CNBC said the Wall Street Journal reported on 17 November that the SEC is probing Nvidia amid Jensen Huang's departure. What the probe covers is not yet known.

steps.text: Export controls work at the border: a seller needs a licence to ship advanced chips to China.
Back door one: a buyer in a third country buys chips legally, then passes them on. This is diversion.
Back door two: the chips never move. A Chinese firm rents computing time on servers abroad, over the internet.
So the 16 November rule targets both: extra licensing for five risky countries, and named end users at data centres.
A BIS rule can be changed later; a law is harder to undo, which is why Lawler's bill still matters.

history.text:
The story begins in August 2022. The US announced export restrictions and licence requirements aimed at China's chip and supercomputing industries. From then on, top-end AI chips could not be sold to China freely.

Nvidia responded with the H20, a cut-down chip built for China. It sold about one million of them to Chinese customers in 2024. The controls changed what was sold, but sales continued.

In April 2025 the US required a licence for H20 exports to China, including Hong Kong and Macau. Then policy loosened. From August 2025 some H20 licences were granted, and President Trump approved sales with a 25% fee. On 8 December 2025 the stronger H200 was allowed to China with a 25% surcharge. Nvidia's newer Blackwell chips stayed restricted. On 13 January 2026 the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) issued H200 licensing guidelines.

Congress focused on a different gap: using chips over the cloud. In January 2026 the House passed the Remote Access Security Act 369–22. It still needed the Senate.

In November 2026 the focus moved to resale. The New York Times reported that Commerce halted its inquiry into Megaspeed after Nvidia's general counsel contacted case agents. The case moved to the Justice Department. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing. The 16 November rule targets both gaps: resale and rental.

lesson.concept: How export controls work, and how firms get around them
lesson.big_idea: An export control makes a seller get a government licence before certain goods go to certain buyers. Firms get around it by reselling through third countries or renting chips remotely, so rules must chase both routes.

steps.title: A licence before shipping
steps.text: An export control says: before you send certain goods to certain buyers, ask the government. For US chips, BIS runs this. Since August 2022, advanced chips for China have needed a licence.

steps.title: Back door one: resale
steps.text: A buyer in a third country can buy chips legally and pass them on to China. This is diversion. The new rule adds licensing for five countries it treats as higher risk.

steps.title: Back door two: renting
steps.text: Chips need not travel. A Chinese firm can rent computing time on servers abroad, over the internet. Nothing crosses China's border, so a shipping licence alone does not catch it.

steps.title: Closing it: know the user
steps.text: The 16 November rule makes overseas data centres serving companies in China, Russia, Iran and Cuba identify their end users. The check moves from the border to the customer list.

steps.title: Rule versus law
steps.text: A BIS rule can be rewritten by a later administration. A law needs Congress. Lawler's remote-access bill has passed the House but still needs the Senate.

stories.headline: Trump seeks nuclear talks with Xi and Putin as APEC opens
stories.question: What does Trump want from Xi and Putin as APEC opens in Shenzhen?
stories.dek: Mainly, a new nuclear arms deal that includes China. The White House says it expects no agreement. Still, this is the first time Trump, Xi and Putin will meet together.

so_far.text: Three threads meet in Shenzhen. The first is trade. In 2025 Trump and Xi put steep tariffs on each other, then cut them after meetings in South Korea and Washington. The second is nuclear weapons. New START, the 2010 treaty capping US and Russian strategic arsenals, lapsed in February 2026, and nothing has replaced it. The third is war. The US-Israel war on Iran began on 28 February 2026. It is deadlocked, and the Strait of Hormuz is closed.

what_happened.text: APEC's Economic Leaders' Meeting runs on 18–19 November in Shenzhen, China. The White House has confirmed that Trump, Xi and Putin will hold their first three-way meeting on the sidelines. It says the main focus is nuclear proliferation, the spread of nuclear weapons. Trump wants a new arms deal that includes China. A senior US official said: 'we do not expect to get any kind of agreement.' On 16 November Trump said he may meet Kim Jong Un in China; nothing is confirmed. On 17 November Canada's Mark Carney met Xi in Shenzhen and won tariff cuts. Trump reached Manila that evening, before heading to China.

steps.text: New START lapsed in February 2026, so no treaty now limits US or Russian strategic nuclear arsenals.
Trump wants any replacement to include China, which turns a two-country deal into a three-country one.
Three-way caps are harder to agree, because each power must weigh two rivals at once, not one.
Analysts say Xi is wary of the meeting, and the Kremlin says agreements cannot be imposed on other nations.
So a senior US official expects no agreement, even as the three leaders meet together for the first time.

history.text: The oldest reference point in this story is 1945. At Yalta, Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill shaped the world order after the Second World War. Some Russian figures now talk of a 'new Yalta', meaning a few big powers settling world affairs among themselves. In 2010 the US and Russia signed New START, which capped their strategic nuclear arsenals. Only those two countries were in it. China was never part of it. In 2025 trade became the battleground. Trump and Xi put steep tariffs, which are taxes on imports, on each other. They then cut them after meetings in South Korea and Washington. Other countries started to hedge. Modi met Xi and Putin at the 2025 SCO summit in Tianjin, as China sought better ties with India after the Trump tariff shock. In January 2026 Canada cut its 100% tariff on Chinese electric cars to 6.1%, for a fixed number of cars each year. February 2026 changed the nuclear picture. New START lapsed, so no treaty now limits US and Russian arsenals. On 28 February the US-Israel war on Iran began. It is deadlocked, and the Strait of Hormuz is closed. Trump says he expects to discuss it, along with denuclearization. In November 2026 Carney met Xi in Shenzhen, and China agreed to cut tariffs on Canadian goods. Those measures build on Canada's January deal. Meanwhile Trump and Putin are pushing a three-way meeting with Xi. Analysts quoted by BusinessDay say Xi is wary of hosting it.

lesson.concept: Why arms control gets harder with three powers
lesson.big_idea: Arms control treaties work by setting caps that each side can check. With two rivals, equal caps feel fair. With three, each must guard against two at once, so any cap feels unfair to someone.

steps.title: A treaty sets a ceiling
steps.text: An arms control treaty is a deal on the most nuclear weapons each country may keep. New START, signed in 2010, set such ceilings for US and Russian strategic arsenals.

steps.title: Each side checks the other
steps.text: A ceiling only works if each side can verify it, through data swaps and inspections. Without checks, each side assumes the worst and builds more.

steps.title: Treaties can expire
steps.text: When a treaty lapses, the ceiling vanishes. New START lapsed in February 2026 and nothing has replaced it, so no treaty now limits either arsenal.

steps.title: A third power changes the maths
steps.text: With two rivals, equal caps feel fair. With three, each country must weigh both others together. A cap that feels safe for one looks unfair to another.

steps.title: Where things stand now
steps.text: Trump wants China in a new deal. The Kremlin says agreements cannot be imposed on others, and analysts say Xi is wary of the three-way meeting. A senior US official expects no agreement.

example.setup: Imagine three countries, A, B and C. Assume A and B are each capped at 800 warheads under an old two-way treaty. C holds 300 and has no cap.

lines.label: Old two-way cap
lines.note: Equal numbers, so neither side feels behind.

lines.label: A's rivals together
lines.note: A must now weigh two possible rivals, not one.

lines.label: C grows
lines.note: C was never capped, so no rule is broken.

lines.label: A's gap
lines.note: A feels pushed to build more, or to demand C be capped.

lines.label: C's reply
lines.note: C is still smallest, so it asks why it should cut first.

example.result: A cap that feels safe for one country looks unfair to another. That is why bringing a third power into a two-way treaty is much harder than the original deal.

apply.text: New START capped only the US and Russia, like A and B, and it lapsed in February 2026. Trump now wants China in a new deal, like country C. The Kremlin says deals cannot be imposed, and analysts say Xi is wary. So a senior US official expects no agreement from the first three-way meeting.

practice.q: Suppose C agrees to stop at 400, while A and B stay at 800 each. What is the most A could face from B and C together, and how far is that above A's own 800?
practice.answer: Add A's rivals: B 800 + C 400 = 1,200. Compare with A: 1,200 − 800 = 400. So A still faces 400 more than it holds. That is why A might push for lower caps for everyone, not just a cap on C.

scenes.say: Ab is story ke peeche ka ek idea: teen powers ke saath arms control mushkil kyun hota hai. Treaty ek ceiling tay karti hai, yaani har desh zyada se zyada kitne nuclear weapons rakh sakta hai. Aur har side ko doosre ko check kar paana chahiye, data swaps aur inspections ke zariye.
scenes.show: A treaty is a checkable ceiling
scenes.speak: अब इस story के पीछे का एक idea: तीन powers के साथ arms control मुश्किल क्यों होता है। Treaty एक ceiling तय करती है, यानी हर देश ज़्यादा से ज़्यादा कितने nuclear weapons रख सकता है। और हर side को दूसरे को check कर पाना चाहिए, data swaps और inspections के ज़रिए।

scenes.say: Treaties expire bhi ho sakti hain. Ek lapse hui, toh ceiling gayab, jaise February 2026 mein New START ki hui. Do rivals hon, toh barabar caps fair lagte hain. Teen hon, toh har ek ko baaki dono ko saath mein tolna padta hai. Isliye jo cap ek ko suit kare, woh doosre ko unfair lagta hai.
scenes.speak: Treaties expire भी हो सकती हैं। एक lapse हुई, तो ceiling गायब, जैसे February 2026 में New START की हुई। दो rivals हों, तो बराबर caps fair लगते हैं। तीन हों, तो हर एक को बाकी दोनों को साथ में तोलना पड़ता है। इसलिए जो cap एक को suit करे, वो दूसरे को unfair लगता है।

scenes.say: Chaliye samajhte hain. Maan lijiye teen desh hain, A, B aur C. A aur B dono par 800 warheads ka cap hai. C ke paas 300 hain, koi cap nahi. Ab A ko B aur C dono ko saath tolna hoga. 800 plus 300, yaani 1100.
scenes.show: A faces two rivals, not one
scenes.speak: चलिए समझते हैं। मान लीजिए तीन देश हैं, A, B और C। A और B दोनों पर 800 warheads का cap है। C के पास 300 हैं, कोई cap नहीं। अब A को B और C दोनों को साथ तोलना होगा। 800 plus 300, यानी 1100।

scenes.say: Ab C badh kar 600 ho jaata hai, bina koi rule tode. A ke saamne 800 plus 600: 1400, jo A ke paas jitne hain usse 600 zyada. Toh A chahta hai C par cap lage. Lekin C, jo ab bhi sabse chhota hai, poochhta hai ki pehle woh kyun ghataye? Yahi hai Shenzhen: New START mein A aur B the, aur Trump China ko C banana chahte hain.
scenes.show: Every cap looks unfair to someone
scenes.speak: अब C बढ़ कर 600 हो जाता है, बिना कोई rule तोड़े। A के सामने 800 plus 600: 1400, जो A के पास जितने हैं उससे 600 ज़्यादा। तो A चाहता है C पर cap लगे। लेकिन C, जो अब भी सबसे छोटा है, पूछता है कि पहले वो क्यों घटाए? यही है Shenzhen: New START में A और B थे, और Trump China को C बनाना चाहते हैं।

stories.headline: Bridges hit in Kyiv and Crimea as peace talks pick up
stories.question: Why are Russia and Ukraine hitting bridges just as peace talks gain momentum?
stories.dek: Russia hit two Kyiv bridges, and Ukraine hit the Kerch Bridge to Crimea. Ukraine says its strike answered Russian attacks. Both sides keep up pressure as talks speed up. How much damage was done is disputed.

so_far.text: Russia and Ukraine are at war, and talks to end it have restarted. Less than a week before 16 November, US, Ukrainian and Russian officials met in Abu Dhabi. These were their first such talks in nine months. Days later, on 19 November, Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are due to meet in Shenzhen, China.

what_happened.text: Late on 16 November, Russian strikes hit the North and South bridges in Kyiv, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Heat and water were cut in some districts. No casualty figures were given. Russia says Ukraine struck the Kerch Bridge to Crimea on 16 November and again overnight on 17 November. Russia called it the war's biggest drone attack. Zelensky said the strike answered Russian attacks on Ukraine's infrastructure. Also on 16 November, Ukrainian, US and European officials held their first joint online talks. EU ministers sanctioned 145 Russia-linked people and firms that day. On 17 November, Ukraine's military backers met in Brussels.

steps.text: A bridge is a chokepoint: closing it cuts supplies, transport or services for everyone who depends on it.
The Kerch Bridge is the only structure linking Russia to occupied Crimea, so hitting it strains Russia's hold there.
Russia's strikes on Kyiv bridges cut heat and water in some districts, as allies prioritise energy protection for winter.
Zelensky says the Kerch strike answered those continued Russian attacks on Ukraine's infrastructure.
With talks restarting and a summit due, pressure on the ground can shape what each side demands at the table.

history.text: The story starts in 2014, when Russia annexed Crimea from Ukraine. Russia then built a link to the peninsula that did not depend on Ukraine. That link was a bridge about 19 km long, costing about 228 billion roubles. Its road section opened on 15 May 2018, and its rail section followed on 23 December 2019. In 2018 the UN General Assembly condemned the bridge for helping to further militarise Crimea. So from the start it was both a supply line and a symbol. It is the only structure joining Russia to occupied Crimea, so Kyiv has long made destroying it a top goal. On 8 October 2022 an explosion collapsed parts of the road span and set rail tankers on fire. The road stayed shut until 23 February 2023, more than four months. On 17 July 2023 two blasts, reportedly from naval drones, collapsed a road section, killing two people and injuring a child. That month Zelensky called the bridge a legitimate military target. Each attack showed the same weakness: one crossing with no twin. In November 2026 the bridge was attacked on two days in a row.

lesson.concept: Why one bridge can matter so much in war
lesson.big_idea: A bridge is a chokepoint: everything crossing must use it. If there is no backup route, each day it is shut becomes lost supply, and those losses stack up.

steps.title: A chokepoint funnels everything
steps.text: A chokepoint is a narrow point all traffic must pass, like a bridge over water. Food, fuel, vehicles and people all depend on that one crossing.

steps.title: Count the backups
steps.text: How much a closure hurts depends on alternatives. The Kerch Bridge is the only structure connecting Russia to occupied Crimea, so there is no second bridge to switch to.

steps.title: Losses add up over time
steps.text: The daily shortfall is what is needed minus what still gets through. Multiply by the days shut. After October 2022, the road stayed shut until February 2023.

example.setup: Imagine an island town that needs 100 truckloads of goods a day. One bridge links it to the mainland. Assume a ferry can carry 20 truckloads a day as backup.

lines.label: Bridge shut

example.result: Even a short closure leaves a big gap when backup is thin, and the gap grows every day. That is why attackers aim at chokepoints and defenders rush repairs.

apply.text: The Kerch Bridge is that single crossing for Crimea. It closed to traffic nearly all of 16 November, and again from about midnight Moscow time on 17 November. As in our example, how long closures last matters, not only whether the bridge stands. In Kyiv, the strikes interrupted heat and water in some districts.

practice.q: The same town needs 100 truckloads a day, but now two ferries carry 20 each. The bridge is shut for 5 days. What is the total shortfall?
practice.answer: Backup is 20 + 20 = 40 truckloads a day. Daily shortfall is 100 − 40 = 60. Over 5 days: 60 × 5 = 300 truckloads. More backup shrinks the gap but does not close it.

scenes.speak: Road 15 May 2018 को खुली, और railway 23 December 2019 को। 2018 में UN General Assembly ने इस bridge की निंदा की, क्योंकि यह Crimea के militarisation में मदद कर रहा था। Russia को occupied Crimea से जोड़ने वाला यह अकेला structure है, इसलिए इसे तबाह करना लंबे समय से Kyiv का top goal रहा है।

scenes.say: Phir hamle shuru hue. 8 October 2022 ko ek blast se road span ke kuch hisse gir gaye. Road dobara 23 February 2023 ko jaakar khuli. July 2023 mein, reports ke mutabik, naval drones ne road ka ek section gira diya, jismein 2 log maare gaye aur ek bachcha ghayal hua. Usi mahine Zelensky ne bridge ko legitimate military target kaha.
scenes.speak: फिर हमले शुरू हुए। 8 October 2022 को एक blast से road span के कुछ हिस्से गिर गए। Road दोबारा 23 February 2023 को जाकर खुली। July 2023 में, reports के मुताबिक, naval drones ने road का एक section गिरा दिया, जिसमें 2 लोग मारे गए और एक बच्चा घायल हुआ। उसी महीने Zelensky ने bridge को legitimate military target कहा।

scenes.say: Ab haal ki ghatnayein. 16 November se ek hafte se bhi kam pehle, America, Ukraine aur Russia ke officials Abu Dhabi mein mile. 9 mahine mein aisi yeh pehli baatcheet thi. Aur Trump, Xi aur Putin 19 November ko China ke Shenzhen mein milne wale hain.
scenes.show: Abu Dhabi talks, then Shenzhen summit
scenes.speak: अब हाल की घटनाएं। 16 November से एक हफ्ते से भी कम पहले, America, Ukraine और Russia के officials Abu Dhabi में मिले। 9 महीने में ऐसी यह पहली बातचीत थी। और Trump, Xi और Putin 19 November को China के Shenzhen में मिलने वाले हैं।

scenes.say: Toh bridges hi kyun, aur ab hi kyun? Pehla, bridge ek chokepoint hota hai, yaani ek tang raasta jahan se sab kuch guzarna padta hai. Ise band kijiye, aur uske paar sabke liye supplies aur services ruk jaati hain. Doosra, Kerch hi akela structure hai jo Russia ko occupied Crimea se jodta hai, isliye uspar hamla wahan Russia ki pakad par dabaav daalta hai.
scenes.speak: तो bridges ही क्यों, और अब ही क्यों? पहला, bridge एक chokepoint होता है, यानी एक तंग रास्ता जहां से सब कुछ गुज़रना पड़ता है। इसे बंद कीजिए, और उसके पार सबके लिए supplies और services रुक जाती हैं। दूसरा, Kerch ही अकेला structure है जो Russia को occupied Crimea से जोड़ता है, इसलिए उसपर हमला वहां Russia की पकड़ पर दबाव डालता है।

scenes.say: Teesra, Kyiv ke bridges par Russia ke strikes se kuch districts mein heat aur paani kat gaya, aur sardi aa rahi hai. Chautha, Zelensky kehte hain ki Kerch strike unhi hamlon ka jawab tha. Paanchva, talks phir shuru ho rahi hain, toh zameen par dabaav tay kar sakta hai ki table par kaun kya maang sakta hai.
scenes.show: Pressure on the ground, leverage at talks
scenes.speak: तीसरा, Kyiv के bridges पर Russia के strikes से कुछ districts में heat और पानी कट गया, और सर्दी आ रही है। चौथा, Zelensky कहते हैं कि Kerch strike उन्हीं हमलों का जवाब था। पांचवा, talks फिर शुरू हो रही हैं, तो ज़मीन पर दबाव तय कर सकता है कि table पर कौन क्या मांग सकता है।

scenes.say: Ab players. Sergei Aksyonov, Crimea mein Russia ke bithaye hue head, kehte hain koi damage nahi hua. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov talks par Moscow ki taraf se bolte hain. Germany ke Boris Pistorius aur Britain ke Wes Streeting ne 17 November ko Brussels mein Ramstein meeting mein Ukraine ke supporters ki co-chairing ki. Pistorius ne air defence aur energy protection ko sabse upar rakha.
scenes.speak: अब players। Sergei Aksyonov, Crimea में Russia के बिठाए हुए head, कहते हैं कोई damage नहीं हुआ। Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov talks पर Moscow की तरफ से बोलते हैं। Germany के Boris Pistorius और Britain के Wes Streeting ने 17 November को Brussels में Ramstein meeting में Ukraine के supporters की co-chairing की। Pistorius ने air defence और energy protection को सबसे ऊपर रखा।

scenes.say: Ab numbers. Kerch Bridge lagbhag 19 kilometre lamba hai, aur ispar lagbhag 228 billion roubles kharch hue. Isse Russia ko Crimea tak aisa link mila jo Ukraine par depend nahi karta, aur dono ko jodne wala yahi akela structure hai.
scenes.speak: अब numbers। Kerch Bridge लगभग 19 kilometre लंबा है, और इसपर लगभग 228 billion roubles खर्च हुए। इससे Russia को Crimea तक ऐसा link मिला जो Ukraine पर depend नहीं करता, और दोनों को जोड़ने वाला यही अकेला structure है।

scenes.speak: अगला number, 145। Russia से जुड़े इतने लोगों और companies पर European Union ने 16 November को sanctions लगाए। Russia की TASS agency के मुताबिक इनमें 47 regional banks और 12 oil refiners शामिल हैं। और 9 महीने, यानी Abu Dhabi talks से पहले का gap।

scenes.say: Ab woh ek idea jo seekhna hai: jung mein ek bridge itna maayne kyun rakhta hai. Sochiye, ek housing colony hai jiska sirf ek gate hai. Use block kar dijiye, toh deliveries aur ambulances line mein phans jaati hain, bhale har ghar theek ho. Koi backup raasta nahi, toh band rehne ka har ghanta khoyi hui supply ban jaata hai.
scenes.speak: अब वो एक idea जो सीखना है: जंग में एक bridge इतना मायने क्यों रखता है। सोचिए, एक housing colony है जिसका सिर्फ एक gate है। उसे block कर दीजिए, तो deliveries और ambulances line में फंस जाती हैं, भले हर घर ठीक हो। कोई backup रास्ता नहीं, तो बंद रहने का हर घंटा खोई हुई supply बन जाता है।

scenes.say: Step by step chalte hain. Pehla, chokepoint sab kuch ek hi crossing se guzaarta hai. Doosra, backups giniye; Kerch ke paas doosra bridge nahi hai. Teesra, shortfall yaani zaroorat minus jo pahunch paaya, guna band rehne ke din. Chautha, safety ke liye bridge band karna bhi flow kaat deta hai.
scenes.speak: Step by step चलते हैं। पहला, chokepoint सब कुछ एक ही crossing से गुज़ारता है। दूसरा, backups गिनिए; Kerch के पास दूसरा bridge नहीं है। तीसरा, shortfall यानी ज़रूरत minus जो पहुंच पाया, गुणा बंद रहने के दिन। चौथा, safety के लिए bridge बंद करना भी flow काट देता है।

scenes.say: Chaliye try karte hain. Maan lijiye ek island town ko roz 100 truckloads chahiye, aur bridge sirf ek hai. Maan lo ek ferry 20 le ja sakti hai. Bridge band, toh shortfall hua 100 minus 20, yaani roz 80 truckloads. 2 din band raha, toh 160.
scenes.speak: चलिए try करते हैं। मान लीजिए एक island town को रोज़ 100 truckloads चाहिए, और bridge सिर्फ एक है। मान लो एक ferry 20 ले जा सकती है। Bridge बंद, तो shortfall हुआ 100 minus 20, यानी रोज़ 80 truckloads। 2 दिन बंद रहा, तो 160।

scenes.say: 30 din band raha, toh 2400. Gap har din badhta jaata hai. Lekin colony ke gate se alag, bridge partly damage ho sakta hai, aur repairs ya ferries chot ko kam kar sakte hain. Isliye Kerch ke liye sirf yeh mat poochiye ki woh khada hai ya nahi, yeh bhi poochiye ki closures kitni der chalte hain.
scenes.speak: 30 दिन बंद रहा, तो 2400। Gap हर दिन बढ़ता जाता है। लेकिन colony के gate से अलग, bridge partly damage हो सकता है, और repairs या ferries चोट को कम कर सकते हैं। इसलिए Kerch के लिए सिर्फ यह मत पूछिए कि वो खड़ा है या नहीं, यह भी पूछिए कि closures कितनी देर चलते हैं।

scenes.say: Ab dekhte hain kaun kya kehta hai. Zelensky kehte hain strike Russian hamlon ka jawab tha, aur diplomacy active hai, bhale aasaan nahi. Russia kehta hai damage ya toh hua hi nahi, ya maamooli tha. Ushakov kehte hain Russia ne talks mein Europeans ko shaamil karne par haami nahi bhari. Streeting kehte hain Ukraine ke baare mein koi faisla Ukraine ke bina nahi, aur unhone 2027 tak support ki apeal ki.
scenes.speak: अब देखते हैं कौन क्या कहता है। Zelensky कहते हैं strike Russian हमलों का जवाब था, और diplomacy active है, भले आसान नहीं। Russia कहता है damage या तो हुआ ही नहीं, या मामूली था। Ushakov कहते हैं Russia ने talks में Europeans को शामिल करने पर हामी नहीं भरी। Streeting कहते हैं Ukraine के बारे में कोई फैसला Ukraine के बिना नहीं, और उन्होंने 2027 तक support की अपील की।

views.view: Kerch strike answers Russian attacks on infrastructure; diplomacy is active.
No damage on 17 November; earlier damage 'insignificant'.
Russia has not agreed to Europeans joining talks.
No decisions about Ukraine without Ukraine; support through 2027.

scenes.say: Ek aam galti: yeh maan lena ki Kerch Bridge tabah ho chuka hai. Yeh confirm nahi hua hai. Ukrainian channels daava karte hain ki ek road arch paani mein gir gaya, aur DW ki ek headline ne kaha ki yeh destroyed lagta hai. Russia ne koi damage report nahi kiya. Bridge ki asli haalat ab tak pata nahi hai.
scenes.speak: एक आम गलती: यह मान लेना कि Kerch Bridge तबाह हो चुका है। यह confirm नहीं हुआ है। Ukrainian channels दावा करते हैं कि एक road arch पानी में गिर गया, और DW की एक headline ने कहा कि यह destroyed लगता है। Russia ने कोई damage report नहीं किया। Bridge की असली हालत अब तक पता नहीं है।

scenes.say: India mein aapke liye iska kya matlab hai? In reports mein India par kisi asar ki baat nahi hai, na prices, na jobs, na travel. Phir bhi, jung khatam karne ki talks pichhle kai mahinon se zyada tezi se aage badh rahi hain. Aur hamara lesson Kerch par fit baithta hai: 16 November ko yeh lagbhag poore din band raha, phir 17 November ko aadhi raat ke aas paas dobara.
scenes.show: Reports don't address effects on India
scenes.speak: India में आपके लिए इसका क्या मतलब है? इन reports में India पर किसी असर की बात नहीं है, न prices, न jobs, न travel। फिर भी, जंग खत्म करने की talks पिछले कई महीनों से ज़्यादा तेज़ी से आगे बढ़ रही हैं। और हमारा lesson Kerch पर fit बैठता है: 16 November को यह लगभग पूरे दिन बंद रहा, फिर 17 November को आधी रात के आस पास दोबारा।

scenes.say: Ab kya dekhna hai. 19 November ko Trump, Xi aur Putin APEC summit ke sidelines par Shenzhen mein milenge. Berlin meeting plan hai, lekin date nahi di gayi. Ab bhi pata nahi: bridges ko asal mein kitna damage hua, Ramstein mein kya pledge hua, aur kya Russia table par Europeans ko maanega.
scenes.speak: अब क्या देखना है। 19 November को Trump, Xi और Putin APEC summit के sidelines पर Shenzhen में मिलेंगे। Berlin meeting plan है, लेकिन date नहीं दी गई। अब भी पता नहीं: bridges को असल में कितना damage हुआ, Ramstein में क्या pledge हुआ, और क्या Russia table पर Europeans को मानेगा।

scenes.say: Teen baatein yaad rakhiye. Jis bridge ka koi backup nahi, woh chokepoint hai; har din band rehne par nuksaan badhta jaata hai. Jab talks tez ho rahi thi, tab Russia ne Kyiv ke bridges hit kiye aur Ukraine ne Kerch. Aur 19 November ko Shenzhen par nazar rakhiye, aur dekhiye ki Russia Europeans ko andar aane deta hai ya nahi.
scenes.speak: तीन बातें याद रखिए। जिस bridge का कोई backup नहीं, वो chokepoint है; हर दिन बंद रहने पर नुकसान बढ़ता जाता है। जब talks तेज़ हो रही थी, तब Russia ने Kyiv के bridges hit किए और Ukraine ने Kerch। और 19 November को Shenzhen पर नज़र रखिए, और देखिए कि Russia Europeans को अंदर आने देता है या नहीं।

Trump announced a US blockade of Iranian ports on 13 April and declared the ceasefire 'over' on 8 July. On 15 November Yemeni government forces left Bab el-Mandeb, with Houthis about 60 km from Aden. On 16 November a third US carrier arrived, while Trump sent mixed signals on striking Iran.

stories.headline: Houthis edge closer to Aden as the US and Iran trade strikes
stories.question: Are the Houthis about to take Aden, and is the Iran war widening?
stories.dek: Not yet, but they are closing in. On 17 November, Houthi forces were reported 25 km from government lines. That day, the US struck an Iranian missile site after Iran claimed a drone attack.

so_far.text: Yemen's government sits in the southern port of Aden. It moved there after the Houthis, an armed movement, captured the capital, Sanaa, in 2014 (one outlet says 2015). A fragile truce collapsed in July 2026, and a Houthi offensive began in September. On 15 November, AFP reported the Houthis were about 60 km northwest of Aden after taking two districts. The same day, Saudi-backed Southern Armed Forces said they were pulling back from areas near Bab el-Mandeb, the Red Sea's southern strait, to defend Aden.

what_happened.text: On 17 November, five Yemeni military sources said Houthi forces had reached Khor Omairh, about 100 km west of Aden. They were 25 km from government lines at Qawah. King Salman has replaced the Saudi-led coalition's commander after battlefield setbacks. Also on 17 November, the US struck a missile site of Iran's Revolutionary Guard on Qeshm Island, in the Strait of Hormuz. It called the strike self-defence. Hours earlier, Iran had claimed an attack on a US radar site in Bahrain. On 16 November, CNN reported Iran could be planning an attack on US officials in Washington. Iran denies it.

steps.text: The Strait of Hormuz is unsafe during the Iran war, so Saudi Arabia pipes oil west to the Red Sea.
From the Red Sea, tankers bound for Asia must pass Bab el-Mandeb or sail around Africa.
Government forces left the areas near that strait on 15 November to defend Aden, giving the Houthis more room.
The Houthis also say they targeted the East-West pipeline, so the Saudi route is under pressure at both ends.
If tankers avoid the strait, the trip to Korea grows from 24 to 54 days, raising costs.

history.text:
The story starts when the Houthis captured Yemen's capital, Sanaa. Dawn dates this to 2014; Al-Monitor says 2015. The Houthis are an armed movement. After they took Sanaa, the government made the southern port of Aden its seat. That is why a Houthi push towards Aden matters so much now.

A fragile truce held from 2022. Meanwhile, the Houthis turned to the sea. In 2023, about 9.3 million barrels of oil a day passed through Bab el-Mandeb. Houthi attacks on Red Sea shipping cut that to about 4.2 million in the first half of 2025, according to the US Energy Information Administration.

The Iran war raised the stakes. Saudi Arabia used its East-West pipeline to send exports to the Red Sea instead of through the Strait of Hormuz. That made the Red Sea route, and its southern exit at Bab el-Mandeb, far more important.

In July 2026, Yemen's truce collapsed. On 20 July, the Houthis declared a blockade of Saudi-linked shipping. They began a ground offensive in September. A Saudi-backed counterattack retook Dhubab in October. But it did not clear the Houthis from the area or retake al-Mocha.

On 15 November, Saudi-backed Southern Armed Forces pulled back from near Bab el-Mandeb to defend Aden and break the siege of Taiz. King Salman then replaced the coalition commander, Lt Gen Fahd al-Salman, who had held the post since August 2024.

lesson.concept: How a blocked sea route raises oil costs
lesson.big_idea: When a narrow sea passage becomes unsafe, ships sail a longer way round. Every extra day at sea costs money, so each barrel of oil costs more to deliver.

steps.title: A chokepoint is a narrow gate
steps.text: A chokepoint is a narrow sea passage that many ships must use. Bab el-Mandeb, between Yemen and Africa at the Red Sea's southern end, carried 9.3 million barrels of oil a day in 2023.

steps.title: Danger forces a longer route
steps.text: When a chokepoint is unsafe, ships avoid it and sail the long way. A Saudi cargo from Yanbu to South Korea takes about 24 days via Bab el-Mandeb, or about 54 days around Africa's Cape.

steps.title: Each day at sea costs money
steps.text: A tanker costs money every day it sails: fuel, crew wages, insurance and its hire fee. So more days mean a bigger bill for the same cargo.

steps.title: Divide by the barrels
steps.text: Divide the extra cost of a voyage by the number of barrels on board. That gives the extra cost per barrel, which ends up in the price buyers pay.

steps.title: Long trips tie up ships
steps.text: A tanker on a 54-day trip cannot carry other cargo in that time. With fewer ships free, hire fees can rise, adding cost on top.

example.setup: Imagine a tanker that costs ₹50 lakh a day to run and carries 10 lakh barrels from Yanbu to South Korea. Assume both of those numbers; the voyage times are real.

lines.label: Short route cost
lines.note: Via Bab el-Mandeb, about 24 days.

lines.label: Long route cost
lines.note: Around Africa's Cape, about 54 days.

lines.label: Extra cost
lines.note: What the detour adds to one voyage.

lines.label: Extra per barrel
lines.note: Spread across every barrel on board.

lines.label: Ship time used
lines.note: The same ship is busy more than twice as long.

example.result: The detour adds ₹150 to every barrel in this example and keeps the ship busy more than twice as long. That is how danger at one narrow strait raises oil costs far away.

apply.text: Saudi Arabia has been piping oil to the Red Sea to avoid Hormuz. Those cargoes must then pass Bab el-Mandeb. Government forces left areas near the strait on 15 November, and the Houthis say they targeted the pipeline itself. If tankers are pushed onto the 54-day Cape route, the costs in our example apply. Brent was already $95.34 on 16 November.

practice.q: Same voyage times, but the tanker costs ₹80 lakh a day and carries 10 lakh barrels. How much does the Cape detour add per barrel?
practice.answer: Extra days: 54 − 24 = 30. Extra cost: 30 × ₹80 lakh = ₹24 crore. Per barrel: ₹24 crore ÷ 10 lakh barrels = ₹240. The detour adds ₹240 to each barrel.

Aden is Saudi Arabia's main oil export port
Bab el-Mandeb is the entrance to the Strait of Hormuz
check.why: The East-West pipeline carries Saudi oil to the Red Sea. Tankers bound for Asia then exit through Bab el-Mandeb, or sail far longer around Africa.

takeaways: A blocked chokepoint forces longer voyages, and each extra day at sea raises oil's delivered cost.
Houthi forces are 25 km from government lines, and Saudi Arabia's Red Sea oil route is under pressure.
Watch whether Houthis close in on Aden and whether US–Iran strikes spread after Qeshm.

sources.excerpt: Aden has been the government's seat since the Houthis captured Sanaa in 2014.
AFP reported Sunday they were about 60 km (37 miles) northwest of Aden after taking the al-Maqatirah and al-Madaribah districts.
US launched precision strikes on an IRGC missile site on Qeshm Island... 'in self-defense'... hours after Iran claimed an attack on a US radar site in Bahrain.
Yanbu to South Korea about 24 days via Bab Al Mandeb vs 54 days (Kpler) (search summary)

Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against Washington. Tehran rejects any suggestion it was plotting a so-called dirty bomb attack on the US capital as 'baseless'.

scenes.say: Kya Houthi Aden par kabza karne wale hain, jo Yemen ki government ki seat hai? Aur kya Iran ke saath war phail rahi hai? 17 November ko yeh dono sawaal aur tez ho gaye. Chaliye, step by step samajhte hain.
scenes.show: Is Aden next? Is the Iran war spreading?
scenes.speak: क्या Houthi Aden पर कब्ज़ा करने वाले हैं, जो Yemen की government की seat है? और क्या Iran के साथ war फैल रही है? 17 November को यह दोनों सवाल और तेज़ हो गए। चलिए, step by step समझते हैं।

scenes.say: 17 November ko Yemen ke paanch military sources ne kaha ki Houthi forces Khor Omairh pahunch gayi, jo Aden se kareeb 100 kilometre west mein hai. Woh Qawah mein government lines se sirf 25 kilometre door thi. AFP ne pehle 60 kilometre bataya tha, lekin woh coast par ek alag point ke liye tha. Toh dono baatein takraati nahi.
scenes.speak: 17 November को Yemen के पाँच military sources ने कहा कि Houthi forces Khor Omairh पहुँच गईं, जो Aden से करीब 100 kilometre west में है। वो Qawah में government lines से सिर्फ़ 25 kilometre दूर थीं। AFP ने पहले 60 kilometre बताया था, लेकिन वो coast पर एक अलग point के लिए था। तो दोनों बातें टकरातीं नहीं।

scenes.say: Saudi Arabia us coalition ko lead karta hai jo Yemen ki government ko support karti hai. Battlefield par jhatkon ke baad King Salman ne uske commander, Lieutenant General Fahd al-Salman, ko badal diya. Naye commander hain Saudi chief of staff, General Fayyad al-Ruwaili.
scenes.speak: Saudi Arabia उस coalition को lead करता है जो Yemen की government को support करती है। Battlefield पर झटकों के बाद King Salman ने उसके commander, Lieutenant General Fahd al-Salman, को बदल दिया। नए commander हैं Saudi chief of staff, General Fayyad al-Ruwaili।

scenes.say: Ab Iran. 17 November ko hi US ne Strait of Hormuz mein Qeshm Island par Revolutionary Guard ki ek missile site par strike ki, aur ise self-defence bataya. Usse kuch ghante pehle Iran ne Bahrain mein ek US radar site par attack ka daava kiya tha. US military ne kaha ki drones ko intercept kar liya gaya.
scenes.speak: अब Iran। 17 November को ही US ने Strait of Hormuz में Qeshm Island पर Revolutionary Guard की एक missile site पर strike की, और इसे self-defence बताया। उससे कुछ घंटे पहले Iran ने Bahrain में एक US radar site पर attack का दावा किया था। US military ने कहा कि drones को intercept कर लिया गया।

scenes.say: Toh hum yahan tak pahunche kaise? 2014 mein Houthiyon ne, jo ek armed movement hai, Yemen ki capital Sanaa par kabza kiya. Ek outlet 2015 kehta hai. Government ne apni seat Aden shift kar li. 2022 mein ek kamzor truce shuru hua. Isi beech Houthi attacks ki wajah se Bab el-Mandeb se guzarne wala oil 2023 ke nau point teen million barrel roz se ghatkar 2025 ke pehle half mein kareeb chaar point do million reh gaya.
scenes.show: Oil through Bab el-Mandeb more than halved
scenes.speak: तो हम यहाँ तक पहुँचे कैसे? 2014 में Houthiyon ने, जो एक armed movement है, Yemen की capital Sanaa पर कब्ज़ा किया। एक outlet 2015 कहता है। Government ने अपनी seat Aden shift कर ली। 2022 में एक कमज़ोर truce शुरू हुआ। इसी बीच Houthi attacks की वजह से Bab el-Mandeb से गुज़रने वाला oil 2023 के नौ point तीन million barrel रोज़ से घटकर 2025 के पहले half में करीब चार point दो million रह गया।

scenes.say: Phir aayi Iran war. Strait of Hormuz se bachne ke liye Saudi Arabia ne apna oil East-West pipeline se west mein Red Sea tak bheja. July 2026 mein Yemen ka truce toot gaya. 20 July ko Houthiyon ne Saudi se jude shipping ki blockade ka elaan kar diya.
scenes.show: Saudi oil rerouted to the Red Sea
scenes.speak: फिर आई Iran war। Strait of Hormuz से बचने के लिए Saudi Arabia ने अपना oil East-West pipeline से west में Red Sea तक भेजा। July 2026 में Yemen का truce टूट गया। 20 July को Houthiyon ने Saudi से जुड़े shipping की blockade का ऐलान कर दिया।

scenes.say: September mein Houthiyon ne ground offensive shuru kiya. October mein Saudi-backed forces ne Dhubab town wapas le liya, lekin al-Mocha nahi. Phir 15 November ko yeh forces Aden ko bachane aur Taiz ki gherabandi todne ke liye Bab el-Mandeb ke paas ke ilaake chhod gayi.
scenes.show: From Sanaa to the edge of Aden
scenes.speak: September में Houthiyon ने ground offensive शुरू किया। October में Saudi-backed forces ने Dhubab town वापस ले लिया, लेकिन al-Mocha नहीं। फिर 15 November को यह forces Aden को बचाने और Taiz की घेराबंदी तोड़ने के लिए Bab el-Mandeb के पास के इलाके छोड़ गईं।

scenes.say: Toh Yemen ke coast ki ladai Yemen se kahin door tak kyun maayne rakhti hai? Chain ko follow kijiye. Ek: Hormuz safe nahi hai, isliye Saudi oil west mein Red Sea jaata hai. Do: phir Asia jaane wale tankers ko Bab el-Mandeb se guzarna padta hai.
scenes.show: Hormuz unsafe → oil goes to Red Sea
scenes.speak: तो Yemen के coast की लड़ाई Yemen से कहीं दूर तक क्यों मायने रखती है? Chain को follow कीजिए। एक: Hormuz safe नहीं है, इसलिए Saudi oil west में Red Sea जाता है। दो: फिर Asia जाने वाले tankers को Bab el-Mandeb से गुज़रना पड़ता है।

scenes.say: Teen: government forces us strait ke paas ke ilaake chhod chuki hain, jisse Houthiyon ko zyada jagah mil gayi. Chaar: 15 November ko Houthiyon ne kaha ki unhone khud East-West pipeline ko target kiya. Paanch: agar ships is strait se bachti hain, toh safar lamba hota hai aur oil mehenga padta hai.
scenes.show: Pipeline and strait both under pressure
scenes.speak: तीन: government forces उस strait के पास के इलाके छोड़ चुकी हैं, जिससे Houthiyon को ज़्यादा जगह मिल गई। चार: 15 November को Houthiyon ने कहा कि उन्होंने खुद East-West pipeline को target किया। पाँच: अगर ships इस strait से बचती हैं, तो सफ़र लंबा होता है और oil महंगा पड़ता है।

scenes.say: Ab players. Houthi, jo Aden ki taraf badh rahe hain. Saudi-backed Southern Armed Forces, jo use bachane ke liye peeche hat rahi hain. General Fayyad al-Ruwaili, coalition ke naye commander. Donald Trump, jo Iran ko warning de rahe hain. Aur Iran ke foreign minister Abbas Araghchi, jo kisi Iranian plot ki reports ko nakaarte hain.
scenes.speak: अब players। Houthi, जो Aden की तरफ़ बढ़ रहे हैं। Saudi-backed Southern Armed Forces, जो उसे बचाने के लिए पीछे हट रही हैं। General Fayyad al-Ruwaili, coalition के नए commander। Donald Trump, जो Iran को warning दे रहे हैं। और Iran के foreign minister Abbas Araghchi, जो किसी Iranian plot की reports को नकारते हैं।

scenes.say: Ab numbers. Brent crude, yaani duniya ka main oil price, 16 November ko pachaanve dollar aur chauntees cent ek barrel tha. War se pehle, February ke aakhir mein, yeh kareeb 72 dollar tha. Matlab kareeb ek-tihaai zyada.
scenes.speak: अब numbers। Brent crude, यानी दुनिया का main oil price, 16 November को पचानवे dollar और चौंतीस cent एक barrel था। War से पहले, February के आख़िर में, यह करीब 72 dollar था। मतलब करीब एक-तिहाई ज़्यादा।

scenes.say: Ab detour ki keemat. Yanbu se South Korea jaane wala Saudi cargo Bab el-Mandeb ke raaste kareeb 24 din leta hai. Africa ke Cape ke around, kareeb 54 din. Yaani do guna se bhi zyada.
scenes.speak: अब detour की कीमत। Yanbu से South Korea जाने वाला Saudi cargo Bab el-Mandeb के रास्ते करीब 24 दिन लेता है। Africa के Cape के around, करीब 54 दिन। यानी दो गुना से भी ज़्यादा।

scenes.say: Isi se aate hain big idea par: ek blocked sea route oil ki cost kaise badhata hai. Chokepoint ek tang raasta hai jisse bahut saare ships ko guzarna padta hai. Agar woh unsafe ho jaye, toh ships lamba raasta lete hain. Aur samundar mein har extra din ka kharcha hota hai: fuel, crew, insurance aur hire fees.
scenes.show: Longer route = more days = higher cost
scenes.speak: इसी से आते हैं big idea पर: एक blocked sea route oil की cost कैसे बढ़ाता है। Chokepoint एक तंग रास्ता है जिससे बहुत सारे ships को गुज़रना पड़ता है। अगर वो unsafe हो जाए, तो ships लंबा रास्ता लेते हैं। और समुंदर में हर extra दिन का खर्चा होता है: fuel, crew, insurance और hire fees।

scenes.say: Ab is extra bill ko ship par lade barrels mein baant dijiye. Yahi hai extra cost per barrel, jo aakhir mein buyers chukate hain. Ek doosra effect bhi hai. Lambe safar par gaye ships doosra cargo nahi utha sakte, toh kam ships free rehte hain, aur hire fees badh sakti hain.
scenes.show: Extra cost ÷ barrels = cost per barrel
scenes.speak: अब इस extra bill को ship पर लदे barrels में बाँट दीजिए। यही है extra cost per barrel, जो आख़िर में buyers चुकाते हैं। एक दूसरा effect भी है। लंबे सफ़र पर गए ships दूसरा cargo नहीं उठा सकते, तो कम ships free रहते हैं, और hire fees बढ़ सकती हैं।

scenes.say: Chaliye hisaab lagate hain. Maan lijiye ek tanker ka kharcha 50 lakh rupaye roz hai, aur woh 10 lakh barrel le jaata hai. Yeh dono numbers assume kiye gaye hain. Bab el-Mandeb ke raaste, 24 din ka kharcha 12 crore rupaye. Cape ke around, 54 din ka kharcha 27 crore.
scenes.speak: चलिए हिसाब लगाते हैं। मान लीजिए एक tanker का खर्चा 50 लाख रुपये रोज़ है, और वो 10 लाख barrel ले जाता है। यह दोनों numbers assume किए गए हैं। Bab el-Mandeb के रास्ते, 24 दिन का खर्चा 12 करोड़ रुपये। Cape के around, 54 दिन का खर्चा 27 करोड़।

scenes.say: Ab ghataiye. 27 crore minus 12 crore, yaani ek voyage ke liye 15 crore extra. Ise 10 lakh barrel mein baantiye, toh har barrel 150 rupaye mehenga padta hai. Aur ship sawa do guna zyada time busy rehta hai.
scenes.speak: अब घटाइए। 27 करोड़ minus 12 करोड़, यानी एक voyage के लिए 15 करोड़ extra। इसे 10 लाख barrel में बाँटिए, तो हर barrel 150 रुपये महंगा पड़ता है। और ship सवा दो गुना ज़्यादा time busy रहता है।

scenes.say: Ab Iran wala dispute. 16 November ko CNN ne report kiya ki Iran Washington mein US officials par dirty bomb ya chemical attack ki planning kar sakta hai. Trump kehte hain ki woh ise bahut seriously le rahe hain, aur warning di ki aisi keemat chukani padegi jo kisi desh ne kabhi nahi chukayi. Iran ke foreign minister ne reports ko bakwaas bataya aur Israel par ilzaam lagaya.
scenes.show: A reported plot, and a flat denial
scenes.speak: अब Iran वाला dispute। 16 November को CNN ने report किया कि Iran Washington में US officials पर dirty bomb या chemical attack की planning कर सकता है। Trump कहते हैं कि वो इसे बहुत seriously ले रहे हैं, और warning दी कि ऐसी कीमत चुकानी पड़ेगी जो किसी देश ने कभी नहीं चुकाई। Iran के foreign minister ने reports को बकवास बताया और Israel पर इल्ज़ाम लगाया।

scenes.say: Lekin ise aisa attack mat samjhiye jo bas hone hi wala hai. CNN ke sources ne kaha ki yeh planning Iran ko options dene ke baare mein thi, kisi imminent attack ka sign nahi. White House spokesperson Lauren Bis kehti hain ki is samay homeland ko koi credible threat nahi hai. Anonymous sources ke alawa koi saboot public nahi hai.
scenes.speak: लेकिन इसे ऐसा attack मत समझिए जो बस होने ही वाला है। CNN के sources ने कहा कि यह planning Iran को options देने के बारे में थी, किसी imminent attack का sign नहीं। White House spokesperson Lauren Bis कहती हैं कि इस समय homeland को कोई credible threat नहीं है। Anonymous sources के अलावा कोई सबूत public नहीं है।

scenes.say: Yemen par analyst Mohammed Al-Qadhi Bab el-Mandeb se withdrawal ko ek bada setback kehte hain, aur kehte hain ki Houthi kareeb aur kareeb aa rahe hain. Analyst Umar Karim kehte hain ki naya commander structural problems theek kar paaye, iski ummeed kam hai, jab tak woh bahut hi competent na ho.
scenes.show: Analysts: a setback, and deeper problems
scenes.speak: Yemen पर analyst Mohammed Al-Qadhi Bab el-Mandeb से withdrawal को एक बड़ा setback कहते हैं, और कहते हैं कि Houthi करीब और करीब आ रहे हैं। Analyst Umar Karim कहते हैं कि नया commander structural problems ठीक कर पाए, इसकी उम्मीद कम है, जब तक वो बहुत ही competent न हो।

scenes.say: India mein aapke liye iska kya matlab hai? July mein data firm Kpler ne kaha ki Houthi blockade se shayad India ko sabse zyada chot lag sakti hai, kyunki uske aadhe se zyada crude imports Bab el-Mandeb se guzarte hain. Jaisa humare example mein dikha, Africa ke around detour har barrel ki cost badhata hai. Kya yeh Indian petrol pump ki keemat tak pahunchega, yeh abhi pata nahi.
scenes.show: Over half India's crude passes Bab el-Mandeb
scenes.speak: India में आपके लिए इसका क्या मतलब है? July में data firm Kpler ने कहा कि Houthi blockade से शायद India को सबसे ज़्यादा चोट लग सकती है, क्योंकि उसके आधे से ज़्यादा crude imports Bab el-Mandeb से गुज़रते हैं। जैसा हमारे example में दिखा, Africa के around detour हर barrel की cost बढ़ाता है। क्या यह Indian petrol pump की कीमत तक पहुँचेगा, यह अभी पता नहीं।

scenes.say: Aage kya dekhna hai? Kya Houthi forces Qawah mein 25 kilometre ka gap band karengi, aur kya woh Aden tak pahunch bhi paayengi? Kya naye commander coalition ko sambhaal paayenge? Kya Qeshm strike aur badi US strikes ka ishaara hai? Aur kya Saudi shipping blockade ab bhi laagu hai? Abhi hum nahi jaante.

scenes.speak: आगे क्या देखना है? क्या Houthi forces Qawah में 25 kilometre का gap बंद करेंगी, और क्या वो Aden तक पहुँच भी पाएँगी? क्या नए commander coalition को संभाल पाएँगे? क्या Qeshm strike और बड़ी US strikes का इशारा है? और क्या Saudi shipping blockade अब भी लागू है? अभी हम नहीं जानते।

Do: Houthi forces government lines se 25 kilometre door hain, aur Saudi Arabia ka Red Sea oil route pressure mein hai. stories.headline: Supreme Court bails two Bilkis Bano convicts; she says she wasn't heard
stories.question: Why did the Supreme Court bail two Bilkis Bano convicts without hearing her?
stories.dek: Two judges said more than 17 years in custody, one convict's severe disability and arguable appeals justified bail. Bilkis Bano says no one told her or heard her, and she will fight the order.

so_far.text: In 2002, during the Gujarat riots, Bilkis Bano was gang-raped, and seven of her family members were murdered. In 2008 a Mumbai court gave 11 men life sentences. Gujarat released them early in August 2022. The Supreme Court cancelled that release in January 2024, and the men went back to jail. Two of them, Bipinchand Joshi and Pradip Modhiya, are appealing their convictions in the Supreme Court.

what_happened.text: On 28 October 2026, Supreme Court Justices M M Sundresh and P B Varale granted bail to Joshi and Modhiya until their appeals are decided. The bench cited more than 17 years in custody, Joshi's severe handicap, and issues of fact and law in the appeals. It noted one man was not named in the first police report (FIR) and was implicated nearly three years later. The Additional Solicitor General opposed bail, citing the seriousness of the offences. The order was widely reported only on 16 November. Reports on 17 November said Bilkis Bano was not informed or heard, and that she will fight the order.

steps.text: An appeal against a conviction can take years, so a higher court may release a convict on bail while it waits.
Judges weigh time served, health and arguable appeal points: here, over 17 years, a severe handicap, and doubts about one man's FIR.
Against that sits the seriousness of the crime, which is why the Additional Solicitor General opposed bail.
In a criminal appeal, the formal sides are usually the convict and the State, so a victim is not automatically in court.
Bilkis Bano says she was neither informed nor heard; the reports do not say why the bench did not hear her.

history.text: The story begins in 2002. During the Gujarat riots, Bilkis Bano, then 21 and three months pregnant, was gang-raped. Seven of her family members were murdered, including her three-year-old daughter. In December 2003 the Supreme Court handed the investigation to the CBI, the central investigating agency. In 2004, after death threats, it moved the trial out of Gujarat to Maharashtra. Which state held the trial mattered later. In 2008 a Mumbai court convicted 11 men and sentenced them to life. On 4 May 2017 the Bombay High Court upheld the convictions of Joshi and Modhiya, who then appealed to the Supreme Court. Next came a fight over remission, meaning early release ordered by a government. On 13 May 2022 the Supreme Court treated Gujarat as the government that could decide. On 15 August 2022 Gujarat freed all 11 men under its 1992 remission policy. Bilkis Bano asked the court to review the May ruling. That request was dismissed on 13 December 2022, decided in chambers without lawyers arguing, as review petitions normally are. On 8 January 2024 Justices B V Nagarathna and Ujjal Bhuyan cancelled the remission. They ruled that Maharashtra, where the trial was held, was the right government to decide. The 11 men surrendered at Godhra sub-jail that month. In March 2026 the Supreme Court issued notice on the two men's appeals, formally asking the other side to respond.

lesson.concept: How bail works while a conviction is under appeal
lesson.big_idea: Appeals against a conviction can take years. So a higher court may release the convict on bail meanwhile. The conviction still stands; bail only pauses the jail time until the appeal is decided.

steps.title: Conviction, then appeal
steps.text: A trial court decides guilt and the sentence. The convict can ask a higher court to look again. Here, a Mumbai court convicted 11 men in 2008, and the Bombay High Court upheld two of the convictions in 2017.

steps.title: Appeals take time
steps.text: Higher courts have long queues, so an appeal can wait years for its final hearing. If the convict is later found innocent, the jail time served meanwhile can never be given back.

steps.title: What the judges weigh
steps.text: For bail pending appeal, judges weigh time already served, health, and whether the appeal raises arguable points. Against these, they weigh how serious the crime is and any risk to victims or witnesses.

steps.title: Bail is not acquittal
steps.text: Acquittal means being cleared. Bail is different: the conviction stays, and only the jail time pauses. The trial court usually sets conditions, as it will here. If the appeal fails, the convict goes back to jail.

steps.title: Who is in the room
steps.text: In a criminal appeal, the formal sides are usually the convict and the State, which prosecutes the case. A victim is not automatically a party, so whether she is told and heard becomes a real question.

example.result: Bail pending appeal is a balance. Long time served and a serious appeal push towards release. A grave crime and risk to the victim push against it. The conviction is untouched either way.

apply.text: In this case the bench found the balance tipped towards bail: over 17 years in custody, Joshi's severe handicap, and appeals raising issues of fact and law. The Additional Solicitor General pushed the other way, citing the seriousness of the offences. Bilkis Bano says the person most affected, the survivor, was never asked.

practice.q: Another convict has served 2 years. His appeal raises no new point of fact or law, and his crime is grave. Is bail pending appeal likely?
practice.answer: Step 1: time served is short, only 2 years, so little weighs for him. Step 2: no arguable point, so the appeal looks weak. Step 3: the crime is grave, which weighs against. All three point the same way, so bail is unlikely.

scenes.say: Toh ab bail kyun? Pehli baat, appeal mein saalon lag sakte hain, isliye upar ki court intezaar ke dauraan convict ko release kar sakti hai. scenes.speak: तो अब bail क्यों? पहली बात, appeal में सालों लग सकते हैं, इसलिए ऊपर की court इंतज़ार के दौरान convict को release कर सकती है। दूसरी, judges देखते हैं कितनी सज़ा काट ली, health कैसी है, और appeal में arguable points हैं या नहीं। यहाँ इसका मतलब था 17 साल से ज़्यादा, severe handicap, और एक आदमी की FIR पर शक।

Chauthi, criminal appeal mein formal sides aam taur par convict aur State hote hain. Victim apne aap court mein nahi hoti. Reports yeh nahi batati ki bench ne unki baat kyun nahi suni.
scenes.speak: तीसरी बात, इन सब के सामने है crime कितना serious है। इसी वजह से Additional Solicitor General ने bail oppose की। चौथी, criminal appeal में formal sides आम तौर पर convict और State होते हैं। Victim अपने आप court में नहीं होती। Reports यह नहीं बतातीं कि bench ने उनकी बात क्यों नहीं सुनी।

Lekin appeals saalon atak sakti hain. Agar baad mein woh begunaah nikla, toh is beech kaati gayi jail kabhi wapas nahi mil sakti.
scenes.speak: अब सीखने वाला idea: जब conviction पर appeal चल रही हो, तब bail। Trial court तय करता है कि कोई guilty है या नहीं। Convict ऊपर की court से दोबारा देखने को कह सकता है। लेकिन appeals सालों अटक सकती हैं। अगर बाद में वो बेगुनाह निकला, तो इस बीच काटी गई jail कभी वापस नहीं मिल सकती।

scenes.say: Isliye judges dekhte hain kitni saza kaat li, health, aur appeal kitni mazboot lagti hai. Doosri taraf, woh crime kitna serious hai aur victims ko kitna khatra hai, yeh bhi tolte hain. Bail acquittal nahi hai. Conviction bani rehti hai, bas jail ruk jaati hai. Aur kyunki formal sides convict aur State hain, ho sakta hai victim us kamre mein ho hi nahi.
scenes.speak: इसलिए judges देखते हैं कितनी सज़ा काट ली, health, और appeal कितनी मज़बूत लगती है। दूसरी तरफ, वो crime कितना serious है और victims को कितना खतरा है, यह भी तोलते हैं। Bail acquittal नहीं है। Conviction बनी रहती है, बस jail रुक जाती है। और क्योंकि formal sides convict और State हैं, हो सकता है victim उस कमरे में हो ही नहीं।

scenes.say: Ab doosra pehlu. Kya crime bahut serious hai? Kya victim ko khatra hai? Yeh baatein bail ke khilaaf jaati hain. Agar judge bail deta hai, tab bhi conviction bani rehti hai. stories.headline: SEBI weighs limits on borrowing from brokers to buy shares
stories.question: Why might SEBI limit borrowing to buy shares, and who would it hit?
stories.dek: Borrowing from brokers to buy shares hit a record $15 billion by July 2026. SEBI may cap it to curb market swings. Retail traders who use broker loans would feel it first.

so_far.text: In India, brokers can lend you part of the money to buy shares. This is called the margin trading facility (MTF), and brokers charge 9–18% interest on it. After SEBI tightened rules on derivatives trading, some retail traders moved to MTF, according to Devarsh Vakil of HDFC Securities. By July 2026, MTF borrowing hit a record of about $15 billion, up 50% in a year.

what_happened.text: On 17 November 2026, Reuters, citing sources, reported that SEBI, India's market regulator, may limit leveraged stock bets to curb volatility. Leveraged bets are share purchases made partly with borrowed money. The Economic Times reported the same day that SEBI is exploring such limits as retail participation rises and margin-funded bets sit at record levels. Hard limits tied to a company's free float, the shares the public can freely trade, are under discussion. No exact limits or timeline have been reported.

steps.text: SEBI's curbs on derivatives pushed some retail traders to borrow from brokers for ordinary share trades instead.
That borrowing grew fast, reaching a record of about $15 billion by July 2026, up 50% in a year.
Borrowed bets magnify losses. When prices fall, brokers sell borrowers' shares, and that selling can deepen the fall.
Heavy borrowed buying in stocks like TCS, Infosys and HDFC Bank can make price swings sharper in volatile periods.
So SEBI is exploring hard limits, possibly tied to how many of a company's shares are freely traded.

history.text:
The story starts with derivatives: futures and options, which are bets on price moves without owning the shares. In 2025 SEBI tightened these rules. Reports said it capped single-stock derivative positions at 15% of a company's free float or 65 times its cash-market volume, whichever was lower. Stricter position and monitoring norms took effect from 1 October 2025.

That changed where small traders went. Devarsh Vakil of HDFC Securities said the curbs pushed some retail traders, including single-stock futures traders, towards borrowed money for ordinary share trades in the cash market.

SEBI then turned to the borrowing itself. In May 2026 it rejected a broker body's proposal to cut collateral requirements. It said initial margins 'prevent excessive leverage and avoid systemic risk build up'. In June 2026 a SEBI consultation paper proposed capping each broker's MTF lending at 5.5 times the broker's own net worth. It kept a cap on any single client at 10% of the maximum allowed lending.

The borrowing kept growing anyway. By July 2026 it reached a record of about $15 billion, up 50% in a year. On 17 November 2026 Reuters reported that SEBI may now limit leveraged stock bets directly, with limits tied to free float under discussion.

analogy.text: MTF is like buying a flat with a home loan. You pay a down payment, say a quarter, and the lender pays the rest. If the flat's price falls 10%, the loss on your own money is about four times bigger.
analogy.breaks: Share prices move every day, and a broker can sell your shares within days if you don't add money. Banks rarely sell homes over a dip.

for_you.text: If you buy shares through your broker's MTF option, a limit could cut how much you can borrow. It is not yet known by how much, or for which stocks. TCS, Infosys and HDFC Bank were heavily bought this way. If you don't borrow, the direct effect on you is small.

misconception.myth: Borrowing to buy shares only makes your profits bigger.
misconception.fact: It makes losses bigger by the same multiple, and you pay 9–18% interest. With a position four times your own money, a 10% price fall costs you about four times as much.

lesson.concept: How borrowing to buy shares multiplies gains and losses
lesson.big_idea: When you borrow to buy shares, gains and losses are counted on the whole purchase, but they land on your smaller slice of money. So a small price move becomes a big move for you.

steps.title: Your money plus the broker's
steps.text: With a margin trading facility (MTF), you pay part of the share price and your broker lends the rest. Brokers in India charge 9–18% interest on this loan.

steps.title: The shares become the security
steps.text: The shares you buy are held as collateral, a security for the loan. Your own slice is called the margin. SEBI says initial margins prevent excessive leverage.

steps.title: Moves hit the full amount
steps.text: Buy ₹4 of shares with ₹1 of your own, and a 1% price move changes your money by about 4%. That multiple is leverage, and it works both ways.

steps.title: Falls can force selling
steps.text: If prices fall far enough, the broker asks you for more money, a margin call. If you can't pay, it sells your shares. Many forced sales at once can deepen a fall.

steps.title: Regulators can cap leverage
steps.text: SEBI's June 2026 proposal caps a broker's MTF lending at 5.5 times its net worth, and any one client at 10% of the maximum. Limits tied to free float are now under discussion.

example.setup: Say you have ₹1 lakh. Your broker lends you ₹3 lakh more, and you buy ₹4 lakh of shares. A month later the share price has fallen 10%.

lines.label: Shares bought
lines.note: Your own slice is only a quarter.

lines.label: After a 10% fall
lines.note: The fall applies to the full ₹4 lakh.

lines.label: One month's interest
lines.note: 12% sits within the 9–18% brokers charge.

lines.label: Your total loss
lines.note: Price loss plus interest.

lines.label: Share of your money
lines.note: Without borrowing, you would lose ₹10,000, or 10%.

example.result: A 10% fall in the share wiped out 43% of your own money. Borrowing three times your cash roughly quadrupled the damage, and that is before any forced sale.

apply.text: MTF borrowing hit a record of about $15 billion by July 2026, up 50% in a year. In our made-up example, a 10% price fall wiped out far more than 10% of the borrower's own money. SEBI's proposed cap on each broker's total lending, and any free-float limits it may set, could slow how much borrowing builds up. How much is not yet known.

practice.q: Same ₹1 lakh, but your broker lends only ₹1 lakh. The share rises 10% and you sell after one month. Assume 12% a year interest. What do you gain?
practice.answer: You buy ₹2 lakh of shares. A 10% rise adds ₹20,000. Interest is 1% of ₹1 lakh = ₹1,000. Net gain: ₹20,000 − ₹1,000 = ₹19,000, which is 19% of your own ₹1 lakh.

check.why: The 10% fall hits all ₹4 of shares, a 40-paise loss. That is 40% of your ₹1, before interest.

takeaways: Borrowing to buy shares multiplies both gains and losses on your own money.
Margin borrowing hit a record $15 billion by July 2026; SEBI may cap it to curb swings.
Watch for a SEBI proposal setting the exact limits, possibly tied to free float.

thread.previously: India's inflation climbed through autumn 2026. Retail inflation hit 6.09% in October, above the RBI's 6% ceiling, with food at 8.94%. On 16 November, October wholesale inflation came in at 12.29%. Reuters says fuel is the main driver, and a low October 2025 base (minus 1.21%) enlarges the figure. Economists, including ICRA's Aditi Nayar, call a rate hike nearly certain at the RBI's 2–4 December meeting. The repo rate was last confirmed at 5.25%.
thread.changed: New: sources show the RBI already raised the repo rate to 5.50% on 7 October, so our earlier 5.25% figure was out of date. Forecasters split on one versus two more hikes. ICRA puts 2026–27 growth at 7.1%.

stories.headline: RBI likely to raise rates again in December as growth cools
stories.question: With inflation rising, how many more RBI rate hikes are coming, and how much will growth slow?
stories.dek: Forecasters expect another repo rate hike at the RBI's 2–4 December meeting, but they disagree on how many hikes follow. ICRA sees growth slowing from 7.8% in April–June to 7.1% for the full year.

so_far.text: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) sets the repo rate. The repo rate is the interest the RBI charges banks for short-term loans. The RBI cut it to 5.25% in December 2025. At its meeting on 7 October 2026 it raised its 2026–27 inflation forecast to 5.2%. It also raised the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% and called its new stance "calibrated tightening". Earlier editions said 5.25% was the current rate; that was out of date. The next MPC meeting is on 2–4 December.

what_happened.text: On 17 November, forecasts for the RBI's next moves split. A report in ET BFSI says the RBI may raise the repo rate by 25 basis points at each of its next two meetings. Rediff cites one report expecting a 25–50 basis point hike in December, and another expecting 50–75 basis points in total. ICRA has said since October that it expects one more 25 basis point hike, then a pause. ICRA also put 2026–27 growth at 7.1%, with 7.5% for July–September and a slower second half. The rupee closed at 93.47 per dollar, a seven-month high.

steps.text: Price pressure built, so the RBI raised its 2026–27 inflation forecast to 5.2% and hiked the repo rate to 5.50%.
A higher repo rate makes bank loans dearer, so households and firms borrow and spend less.
Less spending eases prices but slows output; separately, ICRA blames a weak monsoon and inflation for a slower second half.
How many more hikes are needed depends on how long inflation stays high, so forecasts differ: ICRA sees one, others more.
Foreign money lifted the rupee to a seven-month high; a stronger rupee makes imports cheaper, easing some price pressure.

history.text: India's current rules for fighting inflation date to 2016. That year the RBI Act was amended to create a statutory MPC. The MPC got a target of 4% retail inflation, with a band of 2–6%. If inflation stays outside the band for three straight quarters, the RBI has missed its target and must send a report to the government. RBI research cited by Outlook Business finds inflation averaged 3.8% from October 2016 to February 2020. From January 2012 to September 2016 it had averaged 7.3%. The RBI's last hiking cycle ended in February 2023, with the repo rate at 6.50%. Cuts later took it down to 5.25% by December 2025. On 25 March 2026 the government kept the same 4% target and 2–6% band until March 2031. So the goal did not change, but the direction of rates did. On 7 October 2026 the RBI raised rates for the first time since February 2023. The open question is how many more hikes follow.

analogy.text: Think of the repo rate as the wholesale price of money. Banks get money at that price and sell it to you with a markup. When the wholesale price goes up, the shop price goes up too, so people buy less on credit.
analogy.breaks: Banks mostly lend out deposits, not RBI money. The repo rate steers deposit and loan rates indirectly, and the effect takes months to show.

lesson.concept: How a repo rate hike reaches your loan
lesson.big_idea: The repo rate is what the RBI charges banks to borrow. When it rises, banks charge you more. People borrow and spend less, which cools prices but also slows growth.

steps.title: The repo rate sets the base
steps.text: The repo rate is the interest the RBI charges banks for short-term loans. Most other interest rates in the economy move with it. After the 7 October 2026 hike, it stands at 5.50%.

steps.title: Hikes come in basis points
steps.text: A basis point is one-hundredth of a percentage point. So a 25 basis point hike adds 0.25 points. The 7 October 2026 move took the repo rate from 5.25% to 5.50%.

steps.title: Banks pass the cost on
steps.text: Many floating-rate loans are priced as the repo rate plus a fixed margin, called the spread. When the repo rate rises, the loan rate rises by the same amount.

steps.title: Dearer loans cool spending
steps.text: When borrowing costs more, families put off big purchases and firms delay investment. Lower demand eases pressure on prices, but it also slows growth.

steps.title: The target decides how far
steps.text: The RBI aims for 4% inflation, within a 2–6% band, kept until March 2031. Three straight quarters outside the band means the RBI has missed its target.

example.result: Each 25 basis point hike adds about ₹2,500 a year to the interest on ₹10 lakh. Across many borrowers, that extra cost is what slows spending and cools prices.

apply.text: The RBI has already moved the repo rate from 5.25% to 5.50%. ICRA's one more hike would make it 5.75%; the ET BFSI report's two hikes would make it 6.00%. So a repo-linked loan like Priya's would rise by one quarter point on ICRA's path, or by two on the ET BFSI path. Separately, ICRA says a weak monsoon and inflation will slow the second half, pulling 2026–27 growth to 7.1%.

practice.q: Same 3-point spread, but Rahul has a ₹20 lakh loan and the RBI hikes 50 basis points in December. How much more interest a year?
practice.answer: New repo rate: 5.50% + 0.50% = 6.00%. Loan rate: 6.00% + 3% = 9.00%. Interest: 9% of ₹20 lakh = ₹1,80,000. Before: 8.50% of ₹20 lakh = ₹1,70,000. Extra: ₹10,000 a year.

thread.previously: A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal became Cyclonic Storm Akvan on 16 November 2026. IMD forecasts severe by the evening of 17 November, very severe by the morning of 19 November, and landfall on the Andhra Pradesh–Yanam coast between Nellore and Tuni around noon on 20 November at 120–130 kmph, gusting 145. Rain alerts cover Andhra, Tamil Nadu, Odisha and south Bengal. Odisha has told southern districts to begin early evacuations. It is Andhra's third cyclone threat in three weeks, after Arnab and Murasu.

stories.headline: Cyclone Akvan slows at sea as Andhra and Odisha prepare
stories.question: How strong will Cyclone Akvan be at landfall, and who must prepare now?
stories.dek: India's weather office expects Akvan to become a very severe storm by 19 November, winds 120–130 kmph, and cross the Andhra coast by noon on 20 November. Its rain reaches far, so Odisha is preparing.

so_far.text: Akvan is a cyclone over the Bay of Bengal. It formed by 16 November 2026, and forecasts point it at the Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Tuni. Heavy rain alerts cover both Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, and 13 Andhra districts are on watch. On 16 November the India Meteorological Department (IMD), India's weather office, advised fishermen to avoid parts of the Bay until 20 November. It also forecast very rough seas off Andhra from the evening of 19 November.

what_happened.text: On 17 November IMD placed Akvan about 800 km south-south-east of Visakhapatnam, moving slowly at about 6 kmph. IMD Director General Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said its cloud bands were becoming more organised. IMD expected it to turn severe by that evening and very severe by 19 November, with winds of 120–130 kmph gusting to 145. It is likely to cross the coast between Nellore and Tuni by noon on 20 November. Odisha has listed about 2.04 lakh people in eight districts for possible evacuation. In Ganjam, 2,730 people had moved to 64 shelters by that evening.

steps.text: A cyclone draws its energy from warm sea water, so it can keep strengthening while over the Bay of Bengal.
IMD expects Akvan to become very severe by 19 November, with winds of 120–130 kmph gusting to 145.
Its outer rainbands may reach 500 km from the centre, so rain falls far beyond the landfall point.
It was moving slowly, about 6 kmph, and a slow storm keeps raining on the same places for longer.
So Odisha, north of the Nellore–Tuni landfall zone, has orange alerts and an evacuation list too.

history.text:
Andhra Pradesh has faced more than 60 cyclones since 1975. The state risks a moderate-to-severe cyclone every two to three years. About 44% of it is exposed to tropical storms, and most of its cyclones form in November.

The root of the story is November 1977. That cyclone killed about 10,000 people, hit eight coastal districts and damaged about one million houses. It is still the deadliest in the state's modern records.

Big storms kept coming. A May 1990 cyclone killed 817 people and caused losses of about ₹2,137 crore. In November 1996 a cyclone killed 1,077, and a December storm that year killed 27 more. So two storms close together in one season is not new.

Then death tolls fell sharply. Cyclone Nilam in November 2012 killed 30 people. Down To Earth magazine credits better forecasting and disaster management for lower death tolls in later storms. In October 2014 Cyclone Hudhud hit Visakhapatnam with reported winds above 185 kmph; reported deaths range from about 40 to 63.

Fewer deaths did not mean no losses. Nilam still caused losses of about ₹1,710 crore. Now, in November 2026, Akvan is heading for the same coast, in the month when most of the state's cyclones form.
